title: Split _usage_report_render.py along a functional seam
objective: _usage_report_render.py was 310 lines against a 250-line cap. The preceding commit took it from 21% to 100% line and branch coverage precisely so this split could be verified against tests that predate the seam. Success means the file drops under the cap, every moved function is provably unchanged, coverage stays at 100%, the test count is identical, and the program still generates a real report.
acceptance_criteria: _usage_report_render.py is under 250 lines and the over-cap total drops (41 -> 39)
Every moved function is AST-identical to its HEAD version - verbatim movement, not a rewrite
All three resulting modules hold 100% line and branch coverage, matching the pre-split single-file figure
The test count is exactly 43 both before and after, summed across the split test files, so no test was lost to a collection glob
usage_report.py still runs and produces a complete report from the machine's real atop/pmon logs
No suppression of any kind, and no re-export barrel in _usage_report_render
out_of_scope: _usage_report_parsing.py and usage_report.py, both still 425 lines and over cap - each needs its own coverage-first commit
Any behaviour change to the report output
The pacman_wrapper.sh source-text test rewrite and the installer deploy-lib work, which are separate tasks in this session's brief
verifier: python3 scratchpad/verify_split.py for the AST-identity claim; pytest linux_configuration/tests with --cov of the three modules and --cov-branch for coverage; pytest --collect-only per file for the test count; python usage_report.py --date <today> for the runtime check; check_file_length.sh --all for the cap; pre-commit run --files for lint.
